newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Intel ahead of earnings.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Intel ahead of earnings.

text.p: Traffic in Intel Corp options on the American Stock Exchange (AMEX) was heavy ahead of the company's third quarter results due out after the close, traders said.

Optimism that the numbers would be strong pushed Intel shares to an all-time high of 108 earlier in the day from Friday's 105-3/8. The stock had been hovering in the 80-area for about a month prior to a breakout rally in mid-September.
While the widespread bullishness fuelled call buying ahead of the earnings, caution over a pullback kept the put side busy as well, traders added.
"I hope this is not a case of buying the rumor and selling the news," said Marty Kearney at PTI Securities.

"They (Intel's results) have a tendency to come in at or a little better than many analysts' expectations, so I don't expect they'll disappoint," Kearney said. "But much of where the price of Intel is going will be based on what the company has to say about chip prices and demand for their product."
According to First Call, analysts' forecast for Intel's third quarter earnings averaged at $1.25 per share against $1.02 a year earlier.
October options, which expire at the end of the week and therefore have high gamma implications, saw a lot of speculative buying.

"That's where you're going to get a bang for your buck," said Todd Salamone, a senior research analyst at Cincinnati-based Investment Research Institute. October 105 and 110 calls were the most heavily traded options on AMEX, with over 5,000 lots each changing hands by late afternoon.
Salamone said implied volatility for the October 105 call stood at 66 percent, compared with the stock's historical volatility, based on actual price movements, of 33 percent.

He noted that while such speculative call buying was usually an ominous sign often followed by a downturn in the stock, he would not rule out a further rally for Intel because it has been forming a very constructive price pattern.
"People's expectations are high, which puts the stock at risk...but given the price action of the stock, maybe these expectations are going to be validated," Salamone said.
With the bond market closed today for Columbus Day holiday, the market was generally quiet, but a few other technology stocks, including Compaq Computer Corp, drew some pre-earnings interest.
"I'm looking this week for a earnings-driven market," said Chris Bookmyer, a designated primary market-maker at the Chicago Board Options Exchange.
"Intel is expected to be strong, and the tech sector has been strong, but I still have a little caution because I still expect a mixed bag (of earnings results)," she said.

Salamone said the way Compaq shares recently rose above resistance at 70, a strike price where a lot of open interest in call options had accumulated, was impressive and that the stock could see more gains in the near term.
Compaq stock was up 1/2 to 72-1/8 in late trade.
